newsitem.title: USA: Intel to extend employee stock option plan.
newsitem.headline: Intel to extend employee stock option plan.

text.p: Intel Corp Chief Operating Officer Craig Barrett on Tuesday said the company would make all employees eligible for stock options beginning with its next plan, which takes effect in April.

Barrett, who is due to take over the presidency this spring and is heir apparent to Intel Chief Executive Officer Andy Grove, told journalists in a conference call that some 26 percent of Intel's employees were eligible in the past year.
Under the new policy, Intel expects more than 90 percent to receive stock options, as employees are required to meet certain performance objectives to qualify for the benefit.

"We think this will further tie our employee's performance to Intel's performance and act as a good motivation tool for the employees and also allow us to continue to do a good job in recruiting and employees who do the best possible job for Intel," Barrett told reporters.

The program makes Intel one of a small number of companies with an across-the-board options plan. Each new participant will get a five-year options grant based on level and performance, with one-fifth of shares vesting each year.

Typical entry-level employees will receive a grant of 50 shares, or 100 shares after a planned stock split in May, with one-fifth of the shares vesting per year. At current stock prices around $150, such employees would receive options on an investment currently worth around $7,500 and could take advantage of any share appreciation above that value. Intel

noted its shares increased in value by about 180 percent in the past year alone, helped by the company's record financial performance at a point when must of the semiconductor sector was experiencing a difficult year.
